events.title: Zengo consumer MPC wallet launched
events.description: Zengo launched its consumer-facing wallet in 2019 using MPC/threshold signing rather than a traditional seed phrase model.

events.title: BitForge Lindell17 key-exfiltration vulnerability disclosed
events.description: Fireblocks publicly disclosed a Lindell17 implementation vulnerability initially discovered in Zengo that could leak key material across repeated failed signing attempts when an attacker had privileged access. Fireblocks and Zengo state that Zengo mitigated the issue through responsible disclosure and that no Zengo wallets were exploited.
events.notes: The public sources do not establish a Zengo app version range or an exact private remediation date, so WLR does not invent either. Fireblocks describes privileged access and repeated signing attempts as preconditions for the demonstrated attack.

events.title: Zengo publicly confirmed BitForge issue was addressed
events.description: Zengo published its response to the BitForge disclosure, stating that its research team worked with Fireblocks and promptly addressed the identified issue and that no Zengo users were impacted. Fireblocks separately confirmed Zengo had mitigated the Lindell17 issue.
events.notes: This event records the public remediation confirmation date, not an inferred patch-release date. No Zengo app version or exact private mitigation timestamp is asserted.

evidence.notes: Primary researcher report: vulnerability initially discovered in Zengo, public disclosure on 2023-08-09, CVE-2023-33242, privileged-access/repeated-signing attack model, and prompt Zengo mitigation with no exploited wallets reported.
